header.title: Growth Marketing Manager, B2B
header.lead: You'll run the engine that brings small and mid-sized companies to Onsurity, from the first search to a signed plan. A small team, a real budget, and numbers that the whole company reads every Monday.
header.punchline: We judge the work by pipeline and cost, not by how busy the calendar looks.

the_role.lead: We're hiring a manager who has built a B2B demand engine before and can show the numbers it produced.
paragraphs: You'll own acquisition for our SME plans: paid search, LinkedIn, partnerships and the website that converts all of it. Not just the campaigns: the budget, the funnel, the reporting, and the two marketers who work with you.

Most of our buyers are founders and HR leads at companies with fewer than two hundred people. They are busy, sceptical and price-aware, and they compare us with a group insurance quote from a broker. Your work has to answer that comparison in plain language.
You'll work closely with sales, who take the leads you create, and with product, who own the sign-up flow. When a number moves, you'll be the one who can explain why and what changes next week.

the_level.lead: Not a title for its own sake. These six are what the level asks you to carry.

rows.text: A channel mix and its budget, end to end. You set the plan and defend it.
The goal arrives as a revenue number. You turn it into a plan by channel.
Your team's work, and the sales and product teams that depend on it.
You decide where the next rupee goes, and stop what isn't working.
If the pipeline dries up, it's yours to explain and to fix.
Your team ships good work on the days you're not in the room.

groups.label: PLAN
bullets: Set the quarterly plan by channel, with the cost per lead and the pipeline each one has to deliver written down.
Size each bet before you spend on it, and agree with sales what a qualified lead actually means.
Keep a short list of what we stopped doing and why, so we don't repeat it next year.

groups.label: MAKE
bullets: Run paid search and LinkedIn yourself until the team can, then review it weekly with real numbers.
Brief and edit landing pages, emails and comparison pages that answer a founder's actual questions.
Build partnerships with accountants, payroll tools and co-working spaces that reach our buyers.

groups.label: MEASURE
bullets: Own the funnel report from first visit to signed plan, and make it something sales trusts.
Run tests with a clear question and a stop date, and share the losers as openly as the winners.
Explain every big move in a number within a week, with what you're changing because of it.

groups.label: LEAD
bullets: Hire, coach and review two marketers, and give them work that stretches them.
Set a weekly rhythm with sales and product so problems surface on Monday, not at quarter end.
Say no with a reason when a request would cost the plan more than it brings.

the_bar.intro: Skills get you the interview. These get you the offer, and they're the things we won't compromise on.

traits.title: High ownership
traits.text: The pipeline number is yours, including the weeks it goes the wrong way. You find out first, you say so first, and you come with what you're changing.

traits.title: Highly motivated and self-driven
traits.text: You find the next most useful thing to do without being assigned it, and you say clearly and early when something is going to slip.

traits.title: Extensive AI use
traits.text: You already use Claude, ChatGPT or similar daily for research, drafts, analysis and reporting, and you still check every claim and number that goes out under your name.

traits.title: Fast, with a floor under it
traits.text: You launch in days, not quarters, and you don't buy that speed by skipping tracking or shipping copy nobody has read twice.

traits.title: Direct and low-ego
traits.text: You disagree in the planning meeting, not after it. You change your mind when the data is against you, and you write decisions down.

ai.lead: AI-assisted work is the default here, not a novelty. We expect it to show up in how much your team gets done.
bullets: Use Claude, ChatGPT or similar daily for research, first drafts, ad variants, analysis and reporting.
Read and own everything you publish. "The AI wrote it" is not an explanation for a wrong claim.
Know where it's weak: pricing, regulatory claims and anything about insurance cover. Check those yourself.
Build the workflow, not just the habit: prompts, templates and checks that make the whole team faster.

items: **5–8 years** in B2B marketing, at least three of them owning acquisition numbers.
**Paid search and LinkedIn** campaigns you ran yourself, with the budgets and results to show.
**Funnel reporting** — you've built the report from visit to revenue, not only read one.
**HubSpot or a similar CRM** set up and kept clean enough that sales trusts it.
**Testing** with a clear question, a sample size and a stop date.
**Managing people** — at least one direct report you hired or grew.
**Writing** that a busy founder reads to the end: landing pages, emails, one-page plans.
**Working with sales** on lead definitions, handovers and feedback that changes campaigns.
**Extensive daily AI use** already built into how you work.
**Clear written and spoken communication** in a cross-functional team.
You've marketed to SMEs or HR buyers before.
Insurance, health or fintech marketing, where claims need care.
Partnership programmes that produced pipeline, not only logos.
SQL or Looker well enough to answer your own questions.
You've built a marketing team's first reporting from scratch.
Experience with pricing pages and plan comparison.

rows.value: Google Ads, LinkedIn Ads, Meta Ads
Claude, ChatGPT — in the daily workflow

assessment.lead: Six dimensions. We index on judgement and evidence, not on how many tools you can name.

cards.title: Plan
cards.text: A real Onsurity growth target and a budget. Where you'd spend it, what you'd cut, and how you'd know by week four.

cards.title: Funnel
cards.text: A funnel report with a problem in it. What you check first, what you conclude, and what you'd change.

cards.title: Writing
cards.text: A landing page brief for a sceptical founder. Clear, honest, and short enough to be read on a phone.

cards.title: Testing
cards.text: A test you ran that failed. What you learned, what it cost, and what you did next because of it.

cards.title: Leading
cards.text: How you hired, coached and reviewed someone, and what changed in their work because of it.

cards.title: Bar and collaboration
cards.text: How you handle disagreement with sales and being wrong, and whether the people around you get better.

items: You want a brand role with no number attached. This job is measured on pipeline every week.
You'd rather brief agencies than run a campaign yourself. Here you'll do both, and the first months are hands-on.
You need a large team before you can deliver. You'll start with two people and a clear budget.
You're uncomfortable working where a mistake can delay someone's hospital admission. That's the seriousness this team runs at.
